subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The World Health Organisation defines health as a state of complete physical, mental and social wellbeing and not merely the absence of what?
questions.explain: The WHO definition used by Edexcel states health is complete physical, mental and social wellbeing and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a component of a balanced diet classed as a macronutrient?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates, fats and proteins are macronutrients needed in large amounts, whereas vitamins and minerals are micronutrients.

questions.q: Why is a sedentary lifestyle a risk factor for coronary heart disease?
options: Lack of activity can lead to weight gain and raised blood pressure, straining the heart
It increases muscular endurance too quickly
It causes the heart to beat too slowly during exercise
It reduces the number of red blood cells produced
questions.explain: Inactivity contributes to obesity, hypertension and high cholesterol, all of which increase the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: A marathon runner increases their intake of pasta and rice in the days before a race. Which strategy are they using?
options: Carbohydrate loading to maximise glycogen stores
Protein loading to build muscle mass
questions.explain: Endurance athletes carbohydrate load before events to maximise muscle glycogen stores and delay fatigue.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor that affects a person's optimum weight?
questions.explain: Optimum weight is affected by factors such as sex, height, bone structure and muscle girth.

questions.q: How does regular physical activity benefit a person's social wellbeing?
options: It provides opportunities to make friends and cooperate with others
It directly lowers resting heart rate
It increases bone density in the legs
It reduces the body's fat percentage
questions.explain: Social wellbeing benefits include making friends, teamwork and a sense of belonging, which are separate from the physical benefits.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four types of guidance in sport?
questions.explain: The four types of guidance are visual, verbal, manual and mechanical.

questions.q: In SMART goal setting, what does the letter 'M' stand for?
questions.explain: SMART targets are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound.

questions.q: According to the inverted-U theory, what happens to performance as arousal increases beyond the optimal point?
questions.explain: The inverted-U theory states performance improves as arousal rises to an optimal point, after which further arousal causes performance to decline.

questions.q: A beginner receiving praise and correction from their coach after a performance is receiving which type of feedback?
questions.explain: Extrinsic feedback comes from an outside source such as a coach, whereas intrinsic feedback comes from the performer's own feelings.

questions.q: A coach physically moves a gymnast's arms through a somersault action to show the correct movement. Which type of guidance is this?
questions.explain: Manual guidance involves the coach physically supporting or moving the performer's body through the correct action.

questions.q: Which best describes intrinsic motivation?
options: A drive that comes from within, such as personal pride or enjoyment
A reward such as a trophy or prize money
Praise given by a coach or crowd
Being forced to train by a parent
questions.explain: Intrinsic motivation is internal, such as pride and satisfaction, while extrinsic motivation comes from external rewards.

questions.q: The 'golden triangle' in commercialisation of sport links sport with which two other elements?
questions.explain: The golden triangle describes the interdependent relationship between sport, sponsorship (business) and the media.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of gamesmanship?
options: Time-wasting to unsettle an opponent while staying within the rules
Shaking hands with an opponent after a match
Taking a banned substance to improve performance
questions.explain: Gamesmanship is bending the rules or using unfair tactics that stay within the letter of the rules but not their spirit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a social group whose engagement patterns in sport are studied on the specification?
questions.explain: Engagement patterns are studied across groups defined by gender, age, socio-economic group, ethnicity and disability.

questions.q: Which is a negative impact of the media on a sport?
options: Match times may be changed to suit TV audiences rather than players
It increases public awareness of the sport
It provides income through broadcasting rights
It creates role models for young people
questions.explain: A negative effect of media coverage is that scheduling and rules can be altered to suit broadcasters instead of participants.

questions.q: An athlete takes anabolic steroids to train harder and build muscle. This is best described as an example of what?
options: Deviance through use of performance-enhancing drugs
questions.explain: Taking prohibited performance-enhancing drugs is a form of deviance, breaking the rules and ethics of sport.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of quantitative data?
options: A resting heart rate of 62 beats per minute
A description of how tired an athlete felt
An opinion about a coach's style
A comment on how enjoyable a session was
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and measurable, whereas qualitative data is descriptive, based on opinions or feelings.

questions.q: Why might a coach choose a line graph rather than a table to present a set of results?
options: It shows trends and changes over time more clearly
It removes the need to collect any data
It always makes the data qualitative
It guarantees the results are valid
questions.explain: Line graphs are useful for showing trends and patterns over time, making changes easier to interpret than in a table.

questions.q: A student records the number of press-ups completed by each member of a class and works out the average. What type of data are they using?
questions.explain: Counting press-ups produces numerical values, which is quantitative data that can be averaged and compared.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE PE & Sport Science (1PE0) specification; Health and Performance
